Luntik two thousand eighteen. What are you looking at? My grandson came over and played!
And what did you want again?
We need your help. We need to send requests to all the archives.
Maybe we'll find some dirt on Samsonov after all.
There's nothing on him at all! You've already checked everything.
That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.
What if there's something there? We want to approach from another angle.
How very tactful! All right, here's Lieutenant Sokolov, he'll help you.
Just don't drag him into anything!
Yes, we already understood!
Mikhail Mikhailovich, I looked at your computer. Your graphics card is weak.
And do you play computer games? As the bad guys?
It relaxes me! And I must understand their psychology! That's all, go!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: a place where old documents are kept

examples.trans: The documents are in the archive.

examples.text: Надоело мне в этом архиве сидеть.
examples.trans: I'm tired of sitting in this archive.
My grandmother lives in the village.
That's better than the old lady.
Yes, but better than the old lady.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'graphics card, video card' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To buy a new graphics card.

examples.text: Михаил Михайлович, я посмотрел ваш компьютер. У вас видеокарта слабая.
examples.trans: Mikhail Mikhailovich, I looked at your computer. Your graphics card is weak.

examples.text: Лунтик две тысячи восемнадцать. Что смотрите? Внук приходил, играл!
examples.trans: Luntik two thousand eighteen. What are you looking at? My grandson came over and played!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'семнадцать').

examples.text: Лунтик две тысячи восемнадцать. Что смотрите? Внук приходил, играл!
examples.trans: Luntik two thousand eighteen. What are you looking at? My grandson came over and played!
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to drag into, entangle, involve (in trouble)
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drag into, entangle, involve', paired with 'впутать'.

examples.text: Только не впутывайте его ни во что!
examples.trans: Just don't drag him into anything!

examples.text: Не впутывай меня в эту историю.
examples.trans: Don't drag me into this affair.

meanings.en: after all, still, all the same
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ё-таки').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
That means we have to dig deeper!

examples.text: Значит, надо глубже копать! Дальние родственники, дедушки и бабушки.
examples.trans: That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Значит, надо глубже копать! Дальние родственники, дедушки и бабушки.
examples.trans: That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: masculine noun that declines like a feminine -а noun

examples.text: Значит, надо глубже копать! Дальние родственники, дедушки и бабушки.
examples.trans: That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tactful, delicate').

examples.text: Какие деликатные! Ладно, вот лейтенант Соколов, он вам поможет.
examples.trans: How very tactful! All right, here's Lieutenant Sokolov, he'll help you.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in

examples.trans: I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'прос'). Common masculine noun meaning 'official request, inquiry' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нужно отправить запросы во все архивы.
examples.trans: We need to send official requests to all archives.

examples.text: Нужна ваша помощь. Нужно отправить запросы во все архивы.
examples.trans: We need your help. We need to send requests to all the archives.

meanings.note: verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'game, play' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это отличная игра! Хочешь с нами поиграть? Бери карты.
examples.trans: This is a great game! Want to play with us? Take the cards.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: compromising material, incriminating evidence (colloquial blend of компрометирующий материал)
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'compromising material, dirt' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all.
To look for dirt on a candidate.

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'computer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он это сделал в компьютере, в фотошопе.
examples.trans: He made this on the computer, in Photoshop.
A new computer stands on the desk.

examples.text: Он это сделал в компьютере, в фотошопе. И он урок сорвал!
examples.trans: He made this on the computer, in Photoshop. And he disrupted the lesson!

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.
That means we have to dig deeper!

examples.text: Значит, надо глубже копать! Дальние родственники, дедушки и бабушки.
examples.trans: That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.
All right, here you go. There, look.
Lieutenant Sokolov works in the archive.

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чальник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boss, head' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive: ни копейки = not a penny

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.en: to send (a person, a letter, a message)
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'править'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to send', paired with 'отправлять'.

examples.text: И бабушку на лечение в Израиль отправил.
examples.trans: And he sent our grandmother to Israel for treatment.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'password' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Сейчас сделаем, Михаил Михайлович. А пароль у вас какой?
examples.trans: We'll fix it right away, Mikhail Mikhailovich. And what's your password?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.
понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: понял? = got it?; понял = got it

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: regularly, or as a general invitation: приходи!

examples.trans: If you change your mind, come back. The job is waiting.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

examples.text: Ты настоящий профессионал! Ты знаешь психологию.
examples.trans: You're a real professional! You know psychology.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слаблять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to relax, unwind, loosen', paired with 'расслабить'.

examples.text: Это расслабляет! И я должен понимать их психологию! Всё, идите!
examples.trans: It relaxes me! And I must understand their psychology! That's all, go!

meanings.note: person connected by blood or marriage

examples.text: Раз вы родственники, давайте сто пятьдесят тысяч рублей!
examples.trans: Since you're relatives, hand over a hundred and fifty thousand roubles!
All the relatives came to the wedding.

examples.text: Вы кто такие? — Родственники! Я её дядя из Армавира.
examples.trans: Who are you? — Relatives! I'm her uncle from Armavir.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лабый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('weak').

examples.text: Он же слабый, сразу всё расскажет!
examples.trans: He's weak, after all—he'll tell us everything straight away!

examples.text: Вы никогда не выиграете! Ваш кандидат слабый.
examples.trans: You will never win! Your candidate is weak.

meanings.note: тебе смешно = you find it funny

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: a regional office of a government service

examples.trans: He works at the main directorate.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: я что-то вижу = I see something
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
